knowledge:
- key_parameters: method=Specifies the outlier detection method in epimutations() ("manova", "mlm", "iForest", "mahdist", "quantile", or "beta") ;; norm_parameters=Function to customize preprocessing parameters for minfi-based normalization methods ;; epi_parameters=Function to customize method-specific parameters (e.g., pvalue_cutoff, outlier_score_cutoff, ntrees, window_sz) ;; omim=Logical parameter in annotate_epimutations() to include OMIM accession and description ;; genes_annot=Logical parameter in plot_epimutations() to include gene annotations in the plot ;; regulation=Logical parameter in plot_epimutations() to plot chromatin marks (H3K4me3, H3K27me3, H3K27ac)
- alternatives: minfi=The package wraps minfi's preprocessing methods (preprocessRaw, preprocessIllumina, preprocessSWAN, preprocessQuantile, preprocessNoob, preprocessFunnorm) inside epi_preprocess() ;; bumphunter=Used internally by manova, mlm, iForest, and mahdist to define candidate regions before testing
- when_to_use: Use this package when analyzing genome-wide DNA methylation microarray data (such as Illumina 450K or EPIC arrays) to identify rare, localized epigenetic alterations (epimutations) in a case-control design or within a single cohort.
- pitfalls: Probes in Illumina arrays are unequally distributed, which limits the regions that can be considered epimutations; using the candidate regions dataset (candRegsGR) helps filter these ;; If no epimutations are found, the epimutations() function returns a row containing the case sample information with NA values for all other columns.

workflows.name: case_control_epimutation_analysis
workflows.intent: Preprocess raw DNA methylation data, identify epimutations by comparing case samples against a reference panel, annotate the identified regions, and visualize the results.
input: baseDir (directory containing raw case IDAT files and SampleSheet.csv)
methy (GenomicRatioSet containing preprocessed case and control samples)
workflows.stages: 1. Preprocess raw IDAT files against a reference panel using epi_preprocess ;; 2. Separate case and control samples ;; 3. Run epimutation detection using epimutations ;; 4. Annotate identified epimutations using annotate_epimutations ;; 5. Visualize epimutations along the genome using plot_epimutations
workflows.code:
library(epimutacions)
parameters <- norm_parameters(illumina = list("bg.correct" = FALSE))
GRset <- epi_preprocess(baseDir, reference_panel, pattern = "SampleSheet.csv")
case_samples <- methy[,methy$status == "case"]
control_samples <- methy[,methy$status == "control"]
epi_mvo <- epimutations(case_samples, control_samples, method = "manova")
rst_mvo <- annotate_epimutations(epi_mvo, omim = TRUE)
plot_epimutations(as.data.frame(epi_mvo[1,]), methy)
p <- plot_epimutations(as.data.frame(epi_mvo[1,]), methy = methy, genes_annot = TRUE)
plot(p)
p <- plot_epimutations(as.data.frame(epi_mvo[1,]), methy = methy, regulation = TRUE)
plot(p)

workflows.name: leave_one_out_epimutation_analysis
workflows.intent: Identify epimutations in a single cohort without explicit case-control groups by comparing each individual sample against all other samples in the cohort.
input: GRset (GenomicRatioSet object containing the cohort's DNA methylation profiles)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the preprocessed GenomicRatioSet ;; 2. Run leave-one-out epimutation detection using epimutations_one_leave_out
